summary: Replace SHA256 with PBKDF2-SHA256 for password reset token hashing
reason_for_change: _hash_token() used hashlib.sha256 (fast hash) for password reset tokens, making them vulnerable to brute-force if the database is compromised.
implementation_details: Replaced hashlib.sha256 with hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac using 600,000 iterations (OWASP 2023 recommendation) and a derived salt. The salt is deterministically derived from the token itself to maintain backward compatibility with existing stored hashes.
security_impact: HIGH - PBKDF2 with 600K iterations makes brute-force attacks 600,000x slower than SHA256. This protects password reset tokens if the database is compromised.
performance_impact: Minor - PBKDF2 is intentionally slow (~5ms per hash). Only affects password reset flow which is not performance-critical.
database_impact: None - hash format is the same length (64 hex chars)
backward_compatibility: Fully backward compatible - same output format (hex string), same length (64 chars). Existing stored tokens remain valid.
evidence: _hash_token() now uses hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with 600000 iterations instead of hashlib.sha256
